app.name: Shopify (Admin API app via Dev Dashboard / Partner Dashboard)

verdict.summary: You can create an app and connect a development store or one merchant store with custom distribution, with no review. Any app that installs on many unrelated stores must use public distribution and pass Shopify App Store review, even if it is unlisted. That review has a one-time fee, a demo screencast, compliance webhooks, an install flow that sends merchants straight to the OAuth grant screen, and a long list of other requirements. Also, once you pick a distribution method you can't change it.
verdict.hands_on_effort: 30-60 min to reach Gate 1 or 2. For a public App Store submission, plan on several days to build and document what review needs (compliance webhooks, listing, screencast, Billing API if you charge, GraphQL-only).
verdict.time_to_first_connection: About 30 minutes, using a development store
verdict.approval_wait: None for dev stores or custom distribution. Public distribution: Shopify publishes no turnaround time. One developer quoted 7 days to clients and said the review took longer (reported, not official).

gates.name: Development store install
gates.unlocks: Your app can be installed on your own development store from the Dev Dashboard's Installs section, so you can finish a full OAuth connection through Composio.
limits: Developers report a quota of about 10 custom apps per development store, and some hit quota errors even below that (community report)
Protected customer data works on dev stores after you select fields, with no review

gates.name: Custom distribution
gates.unlocks: A custom install link for one specific merchant store, for several stores in the same Shopify Plus organization, or for development stores. No Shopify approval is needed.
limits: Only one store, or stores in a single Plus organization, plus dev stores
Can't charge merchants through Shopify's app billing system
The distribution method can't be changed after you select it
A Public-distribution app can't be installed on a normal (non-dev) store until it passes review. Developers work around this by creating a duplicate app set to Custom distribution (community report)
gates.time_to_reach: Minutes after Gate 1 (select Custom on the Distribution card)

gates.name: Public distribution (Shopify App Store, listed or limited visibility)
limits: Limited visibility (unlisted) apps go through the same review as listed apps
Must use expiring offline tokens: access tokens last 60 minutes and refresh tokens about 90 days
New public apps must use only the GraphQL Admin API
Scopes marked 'Shopify approval required' and protected customer data (level 1 and 2) need separate approval
gates.time_to_reach: Days of preparation, then an unpublished review wait (one developer quoted 7 days and saw longer)

steps.title: Create a free Shopify Partner account
steps.detail: Sign up at partners.shopify.com ('Become a partner'). Accept the Partner Program Agreement and the Shopify API License and Terms of Use.
gotchas: Shopify can restrict Partner services if you break these terms.

steps.title: Create the app in the Dev Dashboard
steps.detail: Log in to the Dev Dashboard at dev.shopify.com/dashboard and create a new app. Apps made with the legacy Shopify Admin custom-app flow are no longer accepted for new apps. Copy the client ID and client secret.

steps.title: Set the redirect URI and access scopes in an app version
steps.detail: Redirect URLs and scopes are now part of the app's versioned configuration. Set them in a new app version, or in the auth section of the app's TOML file, then release that version. The redirect_uri must exactly match a configured URL. Request only the scopes your agent needs: a write scope already includes read, so only add both when you need to write.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

gotchas: Developers report the redirect-URL setting is hard to find because it moved into versioned settings.
Composio's default list has 36 scopes. Cut it down, because App Store reviewers can ask you to justify each scope.

steps.title: Choose a distribution method on the Distribution card
steps.detail: On the app's Home page, open the Distribution card. Choose Custom (one merchant, one Plus organization, or dev stores, with no review) or Public (any merchant, with App Store review). You can't change this later, so decide first. If you only need your own stores, Shopify suggests the client credentials grant instead of OAuth.
gotchas: A Public app can't be installed on a normal store until it passes review. If you need to test on a real store before then, create a duplicate app set to Custom.

steps.title: Create the Composio auth config with your app credentials
steps.detail: In Composio's shopify toolkit, create an OAuth2 auth config using your client ID, client secret, and the trimmed scope list. Shopify's authorize endpoint is https://{shop}/admin/oauth/authorize, and it takes client_id, a comma-separated scope list, redirect_uri, and state.

steps.title: Install on a development store and run a test connection
steps.detail: In the Dev Dashboard's Installs section, click Install app for a development store. Then start a Composio connection for that shop. Check that the OAuth grant screen appears and that a token comes back, since the callback has to pass state and HMAC checks before the code exchange.
gotchas: A store that doesn't exist returns a 'Store unavailable' 404 page, not an OAuth error, so check the shop subdomain first.

steps.title: Confirm expiring-token refresh works
steps.detail: Public apps must request expiring offline tokens (expiring=1). The access token lasts 60 minutes and the refresh token about 90 days. Check that a refresh happens before expiry and after a 401. Read the message on any 403: 'Non-expiring access tokens are no longer accepted' means the token type is wrong, while other 403s can mean a missing scope.
gotchas: Custom apps aren't covered by this requirement. Existing public apps lose non-expiring tokens on January 1, 2027.

steps.title: Request protected customer data access, if needed
steps.detail: If you read customer data, go to Partner Dashboard > Apps > your app > API access requests > Protected customer data access > Request access. Select only the data and fields you need, give a reason for each, and fill in the data protection details. Dev-store-only apps can stop there. Public apps must submit for review.
gotchas: You must select a distribution method first.
Fields that aren't approved are redacted.
Scopes marked 'Shopify approval required' (for example read_all_orders) need their own approval.

steps.title: Register for the Shopify App Store and complete the app configuration
steps.detail: Pay the one-time App Store registration fee. In the review page's configuration section, set the app URLs, subscribe to the compliance webhooks, upload a 1200x1200 JPEG or PNG icon, enter API contact details, and add an emergency developer contact (email and phone).
gotchas: URLs and the contact email can't contain 'Shopify' or 'Example', including misspellings or abbreviations.
The app server needs a valid TLS certificate.

steps.title: Draft the listing, scope justifications and test instructions
steps.detail: Draft the listing text, a reason for each requested scope, and reviewer test credentials that unlock every feature. Check the build against the requirements: GraphQL Admin API only, Shopify Billing API or App Pricing for any charges, and theme app extensions for any theme changes.

steps.title: Record a demo screencast
steps.detail: Record the install flow, the OAuth grant screen and the main features, in English or with English subtitles.
gotchas: A missing screencast or missing test credentials is a common reason review fails.

steps.title: Run the automated checks and the AI self-review
steps.detail: Run the automated checks on the submission page; they must pass before you can submit. Also run the 'Pass app review' AI self-review from the Shopify AI Toolkit. It only checks requirements that can be verified from code.
gotchas: Submitting beta builds, apps with errors, or incomplete submissions can delay review or lead to rejection.

steps.title: Submit for review and wait
steps.detail: Submit the app. It moves from Draft to Submitted, Reviewed and Published. If core requirements fail, it moves to Paused and you get an email listing the fixes. Shopify publishes no turnaround time.
gotchas: If you are repeatedly blocked from submitting (cooldown), each new cooldown lasts longer.

steps.title: Respond to reviewer feedback
steps.detail: When the app is in Reviewed status, reply to the reviewer's email to continue. Respond to flagged requirements in Partner Dashboard > Apps > your app > Distribution. If paused, fix the issues and click Submit fixes.
gotchas: Installation, embedding, UI, testing and online-store failures require a full re-submit.

requirements.detail: Set in the Dev Dashboard's versioned configuration or in the TOML auth section.
Required before custom install links or protected customer data requests.

requirements.detail: Part of the App Store review configuration.

requirements.item: OAuth immediately after install, no manual entry of the shop domain, redirect to the grant screen

scopes.scope: read_* / write_* standard Admin scopes (e.g. read_products, write_orders)
scopes.effect: Can be declared without approval, but reviewers may ask you to prove each one is needed. Write scopes include read access. Shopify recommends optional scopes for anything not every merchant needs.
Extends order access past the default 60 days. It must be declared alongside read_orders or write_orders, and Shopify must approve it based on your demonstrated need.
Marked 'Shopify approval required': Shopify must approve the app before you can declare these scopes.

scopes.scope: Protected customer data (read_customers, orders with customer fields)
scopes.effect: Level 1 and level 2 data need a separate review for public apps, submitted through API access requests. Fields that aren't approved are redacted. Dev-store-only apps don't need review.

blockers.symptom: The app can't be installed on a normal merchant store, or the install link only works on dev stores
blockers.cause: The app is set to Public distribution and hasn't passed review. Unlisted (limited visibility) apps still need review.
blockers.fix: Complete App Store review, or create a duplicate app set to Custom distribution for a single store or Plus organization.

blockers.symptom: You need to switch an app between Custom and Public
blockers.cause: The distribution method can't be changed after you select it.
blockers.fix: Create a new app with the other distribution method.

blockers.symptom: Redirect URI mismatch error, or the redirect URL setting can't be found
blockers.cause: Redirect URLs are versioned app configuration and must match exactly.
blockers.fix: Add the Composio callback URL to a new app version (or the TOML auth section) and release that version.

blockers.symptom: 403 'Non-expiring access tokens are no longer accepted'
blockers.cause: A public app is using non-expiring offline tokens.
blockers.fix: Re-authenticate with expiring=1 and refresh tokens before the 60-minute expiry. A 403 without that message may mean a missing scope instead.

blockers.symptom: App review rejects the install flow
blockers.cause: App Store rules forbid asking merchants to type their myshopify.com domain and require OAuth right after install from Shopify. A Composio-style flow where the user enters their shop subdomain may not meet this (inferred).
blockers.fix: For App Store distribution, start installs from Shopify (App URL leads to the OAuth grant screen). Otherwise stay on Custom distribution.

blockers.symptom: Quota error when creating custom apps on a development store
blockers.cause: A reported app-count limit (around 10 by default) that some developers hit unexpectedly.
blockers.fix: Use another development store or contact Shopify support. The reporting thread says support had not resolved it.
Pass the automated checks and the AI self-review before submitting. Each repeat cooldown lasts longer.

composio.note: Composio has no managed OAuth app for Shopify, so you must register your own app and enter its client ID and secret. Composio uses per-shop URLs (https://{subdomain}.myshopify.com/admin/oauth/authorize and /access_token). Add Composio's callback URL to your app version. Cut the 36-scope default down to what your agent uses: write scopes already include read, and customer scopes trigger protected-data review. For your own stores, Custom distribution (or the client credentials grant) avoids review entirely. Public distribution needs App Store review, and that review's install-flow rules may conflict with a flow where the user enters their shop subdomain.

open_questions: Shopify publishes no review turnaround time. The only timeline found is a forum post (7 days quoted to clients, and the review took longer).
No confirmed install cap or rate limit for unreviewed public apps. The 10-custom-app quota on dev stores comes only from community reports.
PKCE support for Shopify's authorization-code flow is not confirmed.
Not confirmed whether Composio's Shopify OAuth flow sends expiring=1 and refreshes the 60-minute tokens. Public apps require this.
Not confirmed whether Composio's flow, where the user enters their shop subdomain, can pass the App Store rule against manual entry of the shop domain.
Composio's default redirect URI (backend.composio.dev) has to be added to the app version. Confirm the exact URL against Composio's current docs.
Only part of the 'Shopify approval required' scope list and the category-specific App Store requirements (section 5 onward) were read.
The amount of the one-time App Store registration fee was not found.
